headline: Atomic Habits: 5 Lessons
caption_hook: Atomic Habits sold over 15 million copies. These 5 ideas are why.
intro_line: James Clear's Atomic Habits works because it makes change small enough to actually do.

lessons.detail: You fall to the level of your systems, not the height of your goals. Design the routine, not just the target.
Tiny gains feel invisible day to day, but 1% better every day is roughly 37x better over a year.
Most habits fail on friction, not willpower. Put the running shoes by the door; delete the app from the home screen.

lessons.lesson: Change your identity, not just your behavior
lessons.detail: Don't aim to run a marathon. Aim to become a runner. Every action is a vote for who you're becoming.
One missed day is an accident. Two is the start of a new pattern. Bouncing back fast is what protects a habit.

closing_line: You don't need a bigger goal. You need a smaller, more obvious first step you can repeat tomorrow.

headline: The Psychology of Money: 7 Lessons
caption_hook: Doing well with money has little to do with how smart you are. Morgan Housel proved it.
intro_line: The Psychology of Money argues that behavior, not intelligence, decides how you do with money.

lessons.lesson: Wealth is what you don't see
lessons.detail: Real wealth is income not spent. The visible stuff — cars, watches — is money leaving, not money kept.
The hardest financial skill is stopping the goalposts from moving. Knowing when you have enough beats always wanting more.

lessons.lesson: Room for error is the point
lessons.detail: Plans fail. Survivors leave margin — savings, slack, low fixed costs — so a bad year doesn't end the game.
Compounding rewards patience over brilliance. The longest runway usually beats the highest return.
Not every outcome is earned. Judge decisions by the process, not just the result.
You don't need a specific goal to save. Savings buys options and control over your time.
People's money choices make sense given their own history and fears. Seeing that makes you calmer with your own.

closing_line: The goal isn't to be the smartest person with money. It's to be reasonable, patient, and hard to knock out of the game.
